body: Rockstar opened pre-orders on September 24 for the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection — a premium collector's box priced at $399.99 (€399.99 / £349.99) that ships on launch day, November 19. It contains eleven items. It does not contain Grand Theft Auto VI.

What's inside: a 6-inch Macca the Gator figure with a twist-open stash compartment, matte black Oakley Frogskins with Prizm Sapphire lenses, a New Era 9FORTY snapback, the Leonida Keys crossbody bag, plus a magnetic mirror, a Chunkee the Manatee shot glass, a collectible swizzle spoon, a razor-blade keychain, an enamel pin set, a sticker pack, and a double-sided poster with a full map of Leonida — the last one being the item lore-hunters will be scanning pixel by pixel.

The backlash writes itself: four hundred dollars, no game. But this is entirely consistent with Rockstar's digital-first launch strategy — earlier this year the studio confirmed GTA VI won't get a standard physical release, opting for code-in-a-box instead, a decision that already drew fire from fans and retailers. And they've run this exact play before: the Red Dead Redemption 2 collector's box also shipped without the game.

The real story is what the box signals. The Oakley and New Era collaborations are doing the heavy lifting on that price tag, and "while supplies last" is doing the heavy lifting on urgency. Rockstar has effectively split the traditional collector's edition in two: the game goes digital, the shelf candy goes premium. Whether fans bite at $400 will tell us a lot about how much weight the GTA brand alone can carry — and you can bet Take-Two is watching that number closely.
Pre-orders are live now via the Rockstar Games Store. If the map poster leaks anything interesting, you'll read about it here first.

Rockstar finally speaks: "heartbreaking" leaks, the Collector's box that won't sell out, and a new mod rulebook
body: Rockstar did something it almost never does this week: it talked. After a week in which 14 gameplay videos leaked from a playable build of GTA VI, the studio issued a rare public statement calling the leaks "heartbreaking" for the team — and, in the same breath, apologized for how long everything has taken: "from getting the game finished (nearly there!)" to sharing official gameplay. The key line for anyone counting down: GTA VI is still on track for November 19.

The leaker, operating under the name "Cyberleek," has reportedly been posting clips daily since mid-August — claimed to be a protest against Rockstar's decision to make GTA VI digital-only — while also soliciting cryptocurrency donations to keep the leaks coming. Rockstar's apology is as much a calculation as a confession: with the game eight weeks out, it needs the leaks contained and the hype channelled back into official reveals. It also tacitly admits the obvious: the studio's long silence is partly why the leak economy thrives.

Meanwhile, the Vice City Collection collector's box — that $399.99 shelf shrine we covered on September 26 — has become a talking point for the wrong reason: it still hadn't sold out nearly 48 hours after launch. Fans slammed the £349.99 price for a box with no game inside and no Jason or Lucia merchandise at all, with community member ben (@videotech) calling "£350... a really hard ask" even for a self-described massive Rockstar collector. Rare air: a GTA-branded anything sitting in stock.

On the platform front, The Verge reported that GTA VI pre-orders are heavily skewed toward PS5 — a claim Xbox CSO Matthew Ball answered publicly, saying Xbox is "very happy" with performance, that the game is breaking records on the platform, and that Xbox's pre-order share matches its console market share. A split roughly matching install bases (PS5 nearing 100 million vs. Xbox Series X|S around 35 million) would be expected anyway — but only Rockstar and the two platform holders know the real numbers.

And finally, Rockstar quietly published updated modding guidelines ahead of launch — a rulebook for GTA VI's inevitable mod scene. Creators can't touch official storylines, missions, or characters, can't mash maps or characters from different Rockstar games together, and multiplayer mods are confined to Rockstar's licensed Creator Platform. It's not a ban — the NoPixel RP deal shows Rockstar wants mods — it's the studio fencing the yard before the biggest launch in gaming history.

body: Rockstar doesn't usually chase you — but the Vice City Collection is getting the full-court press. On September 24, the studio sent a dedicated email blast to newsletter subscribers: "Pre-Order The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection Now While Supplies Last," complete with the full collection artwork. For a company that normally lets a logo reveal break the internet by itself, a direct "buy now" email for merch is genuinely unusual.

The timing is pointed. Stock trackers confirmed the $399.99 box was still available for pre-order on September 25 — nearly 48 hours after launch, rare air for anything with a GTA logo on it. Today, the Rockstar Store page shows the box as "COMING SOON." Either the first pre-order allocation quietly closed behind that "while supplies last" framing, or Rockstar is staging the next wave. Either way, the email's job is clear: convert the fence-sitters.

Meanwhile the value debate keeps getting worse for Rockstar. TheShortcut spotted that several items are repurposed from older GTA special editions — the mirror from the original Vice City collector's edition, the swizzle spoon from The Ballad of Gay Tony. And in the purest possible fan response, one X user has already modeled a 3D-printable Macca the Gator figure and is selling the file for €1.50. Four hundred dollars versus a euro fifty: that is the entire controversy in one comparison.
The box remains a Rockstar Store exclusive — one per customer, 11 items, and the game sold separately. If the next pre-order wave opens, you'll read about it here first.
